quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Vendor gives an unqualified IP infringement indemnity covering the Services and Deliverables in favour of Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel (20.1), plus indemnities for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure applies with a materiality-of-prejudice qualifier on notice and a settlement-consent protection (20.4), and Vendor bears the usual procure/modify/replace/refund remedies with no right to terminate unaffected Services (20.5). Customer's reciprocal indemnity is appropriately narrow, limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and Vendor instructions (20.3). Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the liability cap rather than being subject to any super-cap. No redline required.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right; 14.2 gives Customer ownership of Deliverables with an express Vendor assignment and personnel assignments; 14.3 lets Vendor retain Vendor Technology but pulls in the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence (including modify, create derivative works and contractor support) for embedded Vendor Technology; and 14.4 bars joint ownership absent a signed instrument and limits feedback use to generalized suggestions while Customer keeps unrestricted rights in its feedback. Section 15.1 further prevents sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination or model training on Customer Data, and the Customer Data definition captures derived output while carving out only unlinkable telemetry. No assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor and no unrestricted joint ownership, so nothing to redline.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or M&A successor (24.1, with notice and assumption only); Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a direct Customer competitor (24.2); other assignments require mutual consent on a reasonableness standard (24.3); and 24.4 expressly bars any Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control. Section 13 (p0056) reinforces this by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 permitted assignment, and no termination provision elsewhere is triggered by change of control. No redline needed.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, meeting the preferred position. Clause 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer is free to engage any supplier and has made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC or minimum-volume commitment, and clause 2.1 confirms there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining to place further Order Forms is not a breach. The only exclusivity-flavoured restraint (12.4, Vendor shall not market a service competing with Customer's analytics products) runs against Vendor and benefits us, so it is not flagged. No other "exclusive" reference (non-exclusive licence in 13, exclusive jurisdiction in 28.2, exclusive-remedy references in 19/21/30) creates a dealing restriction on Customer.

quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
rationale: Section 13 meets the preferred position on every material term. The subscription grant in 13.1 expressly extends to Customer's Affiliates and to contractors acting on their behalf (plus Authorized Users), and 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, with contractor support permitted. The grant is not revocable at Vendor's discretion: 13.3 limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. Licence rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor under 13.3, backed by Section 24.1, which permits assignment without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or an M&A successor, and 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on Customer change of control. No redline required.

quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on Customer. Section 12.3 expressly confirms Customer is free to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service, engage any supplier and operate in any field or territory, and that no exclusivity or non-compete commitment has been made. The only competition-related covenant (§ 12.4, Vendor shall not develop or market a directly competing service during the term) binds the Vendor and benefits us, as does § 24's bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor. The licence-use restrictions in § 13.4 are ordinary anti-reverse-engineering/misuse terms, not field-of-use or competitive restrictions. This meets the preferred position; no redline required.

quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: Section 9.4 gives Customer an unqualified termination-for-convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days before the effective termination date — matching the preferred 30 days' notice. Customer owes only accrued Fees (no early-termination fee or penalty; the liquidated damages in 7.7 attach to late payment, not termination), and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, reinforced by Section 10.2. Vendor has no reciprocal convenience exit: its termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in 20.5/20 (which expressly bars terminating unaffected Services), and 24.4 blocks a change-of-control exit. This satisfies the preferred position for the three-year term in Section 8.1.

quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
rationale: Section 22 is the only audit right binding us and it meets the preferred position in full: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, require thirty days' prior written notice, are during normal business hours, are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and are at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent (§ 22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars direct access to Customer systems, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material and third-party confidential information, so the walk-away risk (unannounced audits or remote system access) does not arise. Section 22.3 adds further customer protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, shortfall payment resolves the issue). No redline needed.

quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
rationale: Section 28 selects New York law (§28.1) and gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and a carve-out for interim injunctive relief (§28.2). That is exactly our preferred position: an accepted governing law with court venue rather than arbitration. A document-wide search returns no arbitration provision, so there is no foreign-seated arbitration concern. The pre-filing executive escalation in §28.3 is mutual, capped at fifteen business days, and expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so it does not impair our access to the courts. No redline needed.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
rationale: Structurally the clause looks acceptable — the cap is expressly mutual (21.1), the exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is mutual with a helpful direct-damages list (21.2), and the "Excluded Claims" definition (21.3) carves out confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirms Customer's payment obligation is not "damages". The failure is the cap base: "Fees" is defined at 1.5 as only the "Implementation Fee", which 1.6 fixes as a one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form, and 21.1 further narrows it to that first Order Form. The recurring subscription and services charges are therefore excluded, so the cap is an illusory USD 12,000 rather than twelve months' fees — far below the six-month floor and in walk-away territory. Redline resets the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding twelve months or USD 1,000,000, leaving mutuality and the carve-outs untouched.

The second operation was unnecessary and is adverse to us. Nothing in the Fees, Order Form, or General sections obliges Customer to extend Vendor its best terms or to match third-party offers, so the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer) is met. quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: Section 2.1 meets the preferred position outright: there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and declining to place further Orders is expressly not a breach or shortfall. Section 7.1 reinforces this by barring any unstated minimum-use or similar charge, and Section 12 records that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. No take-or-pay, committed-spend, or volume cap on Customer usage appears anywhere; Order Forms (Section 4.1) require mutual signature for any quantity change, and Section 8.2 lets Customer exit on thirty days' non-renewal notice. The Section 22 "shortfall" reference is an audit true-up for over-usage, not a minimum commitment, and the Section 7.7 late-payment charge is a payment-default term outside this rule. No redline required.

Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
rationale: Renewal terms sit at the preferred position: renewals are for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice (well inside the ≤30-day preferred window), and Vendor must give a sixty-day renewal reminder, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed. Clause 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred CPI/3% cap, and adds ninety days' notice of any increase plus protection for prepaid periods. quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.
rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position. Vendor warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1), Deliverables materially conform to documentation and acceptance criteria for ninety days after delivery or acceptance (whichever is later) and Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2), plus no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law (19.3). The remedy is real and tiered — re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure — and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims (19.4). The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or other remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty. Acceptance in Section 6 reinforces this with a rejection/correction and refund path. No redline required.

quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer, which fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs or penalties) and cannot be brought within the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) because it is a payment-delay charge, not a termination fee. At fifteen percent of annual Fees per week it is triggered by a minor breach (a ten-day payment delay) and would exceed the remaining contract value within roughly seven weeks — squarely in walk-away territory. Termination (Sections 9.4 and 10) contains no Customer-payable minimum or early-termination sums, and no other Customer-payable LD appears in the document; the SLA credits running to us are beneficial and are not flagged. Redline replaces the LD with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving Vendor's remedy and remaining consistent with the interest reference in Section 7.3.
